<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:overview}
There is a finitely generated, torsion-free, residually finite Kazhdan group $\Gamma_0$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2em]
\item There are trace-preserving actions of $\Gamma_0$ on a diffuse abelian von Neumann algebra $\mathcal M$, on $\mathcal L(\mathbb F_\infty)$, and on the hyperfinite type II$_1$ factor $\mathcal R_0$, whose crossed products are not QWEP. The action on $\mathcal R_0$ is outer.
\item For $G=\Gamma_0\times\mathbb Z$, there are a trace-preserving action $\beta$ on $\mathcal M$ and a scalar cocycle $\sigma$ such that $\mathcal M$ and $\mathcal L_\sigma(G)$ are QWEP, while $\mathcal M\rtimes_{\beta,\sigma}G$ is not QWEP. The cocycle cannot be removed by a $\mathcal U(\mathcal M)$-valued cochain.
\item There are finitely generated torsion-free nonhyperlinear groups $E$ and $\Delta$ with split exact sequences
\begin{gather*}
1\longrightarrow A\longrightarrow E\longrightarrow\Gamma_0\longrightarrow1,\\
1\longrightarrow \mathbb F_\infty\longrightarrow\Delta\longrightarrow\Gamma_0\longrightarrow1,
\end{gather*}
where $A$ is free abelian of countably infinite rank and $\mathcal M=\mathcal L(A)$.
\item There is a finite QWEP von Neumann algebra $\mathcal P$ and a trace-preserving cocycle action $(\alpha,\sigma)$ of $E$ on $\mathcal P$ such that $\mathcal P\rtimes_{\alpha,\sigma}E$ is QWEP. This cocycle action cannot be changed into a scalar-twisted action by perturbing its implementing unitaries with unitaries in $\mathcal P$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:positiveoverview}
Let $\alpha:G\curvearrowright(\mathcal M,\tau)$ be a trace-preserving action on a finite von Neumann algebra and let $\sigma\in Z^2(G,\mathbb T)$. Then
\[
\mathcal M\rtimes_{\alpha,\sigma}G\text{ is QWEP}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\mathcal M\rtimes_\alpha G\text{ and }\mathcal L_\sigma(G)\text{ are QWEP}.
\]
More generally, the equivalence holds whenever $\alpha$ admits an invariant normal state.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:wreathoverview}
Let $A$ and $\Gamma$ be countable groups, with $\Gamma$ residually finite, and let $W=A^{(\Gamma)}\rtimes\Gamma$. For $\sigma\in Z^2(W,\mathbb T)$, put
\[
\alpha=\sigma|_{A_e\times A_e},\qquad \eta=\sigma|_{\Gamma\times\Gamma}.
\]
Then $\mathcal L_\sigma(W)$ is QWEP if and only if both $\mathcal L_\alpha(A)$ and $\mathcal L_\eta(\Gamma)$ are QWEP.
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
A normalized cocycle action \((\alpha,\sigma)\) of \(G\) on \(\mathcal M\) consists of automorphisms \(\alpha_g\) and unitaries \(\sigma(g,h)\in \mathcal M\) such that
\begin{align*}
\alpha_g\alpha_h&=\operatorname{Ad}_{\sigma(g,h)}\alpha_{gh},\\
\sigma(g,h)\sigma(gh,k)&=\alpha_g(\sigma(h,k))\sigma(g,hk),
\end{align*}
with $\alpha_e=\mathrm{Id}$ and $\sigma(e,g)=\sigma(g,e)=1$. Fix a faithful normal representation $\mathcal M\subset B(H)$. On $\ell_2(G,H)$, put
\[
(\pi_\alpha(a)\xi)(t)=\alpha_{t^{-1}}(a)\xi(t),\qquad
(\lambda_\sigma(s)\xi)(t)=\sigma(t^{-1},s)\xi(s^{-1}t).
\]
We identify $\mathcal M$ with $\pi_\alpha(\mathcal M)$. The crossed product is generated by \(\mathcal M\) and unitaries \(\lambda_\sigma(g)\) with
\[
\lambda_\sigma(g)x\lambda_\sigma(g)^*=\alpha_g(x),\qquad \lambda_\sigma(g)\lambda_\sigma(h)=\sigma(g,h)\lambda_\sigma(gh).
\]
A scalar cocycle has \(\sigma(g,h)\in\mathbb T1\); then \(\alpha\) is an ordinary action. If all \(\alpha_g\) preserve \(\tau\), the canonical trace satisfies \(\widehat\tau(x\lambda_\sigma(g))=0\) for \(g\neq e\), and equals \(\tau(x)\) for \(g=e\).
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
If a finite unitary tuple in \(\mathcal Q_\omega\) has conjugation spectral gap off its relative commutant, that commutant is internal. Consequently, for every Kazhdan group \(H\) and every homomorphism \(\pi:H\to\mathcal U(\mathcal Q_\omega)\), the algebra \(\pi(H)'\cap\mathcal Q_\omega\) is internal.
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
\label{thm:normalization}
If \(H\leq G\) are Kazhdan and \(H\) is infranormal, then every homomorphism \(\pi:G\to\mathcal U(\mathcal Q_\omega)\) satisfies
\[
\pi(g)(\pi(H)'\cap\mathcal Q_\omega)\pi(g)^*=\pi(H)'\cap\mathcal Q_\omega\qquad(g\in G).
\]
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
A countable group \(G\) is \emph{cocycle-hyperlinear} if \(\mathcal L_\sigma(G)\) is Connes embeddable for every normalized scalar \(2\)-cocycle \(\sigma\). For the finite tracial algebras here, Connes embeddability and QWEP are equivalent. In particular, a cocycle-hyperlinear group is hyperlinear.
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:pairprops}
The groups \(\Gamma_0,H_0\) are finitely generated, residually finite, torsion-free Kazhdan groups.
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
By \cite[Theorem~1.1]{EJZ10}, \(H_{\mathbb Z},N_{\mathbb Z}\) and \(\operatorname{SL}_3(\mathbb Z)\) have property \((T)\). Stability under extensions and finite-index subgroups gives property \((T)\), hence finite generation, for \(\Gamma_0,H_0\).

The finite ring maps
\[
R\longrightarrow(\mathbb Z/m\mathbb Z)[(\mathbb Z/k\mathbb Z)^3]
\]
give finite semidirect-product quotients of \(\Gamma_{\mathbb Z}\). If \(S\ne I\), choose \(k\) detecting \(S\). Otherwise, choose \(k\) separating the exponent vectors in a nonzero entry of \(g-I\), and \(m\) retaining a nonzero coefficient. Thus \(\Gamma_{\mathbb Z}\), and its subgroups, are residually finite.

An integral matrix of finite order congruent to \(I\) modulo \(3\) equals \(I\). Otherwise a nontrivial prime-order power would satisfy
\[
0=(I+3^aB)^p-I
=p3^aB+\sum_{j=2}^p\binom pj3^{aj}B^j,
\qquad a\geq1,\quad B\not\equiv0\pmod3,
\]
where the first term has strictly smaller minimum \(3\)-adic valuation than the remaining terms.

If \((g,S)\in\Gamma_0\) has finite order, it follows that \(S=I\) and \(g(1,1,1)=I\). Under the injection
\[
\mathbb Q[x_1^{\pm1},x_2^{\pm1},x_3^{\pm1}]
\hookrightarrow\mathbb Q[[y_1,y_2,y_3]],\qquad x_i\mapsto1+y_i,
\]
a first nonzero homogeneous term \(C_d\) of \(g-I\) would give
\[
g^m=I+mC_d+\text{terms of degree greater than }d\ne I.
\]
Hence \(g=I\), proving torsion-freeness.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:monoid}
If a submonoid \(P\subset G\) generates \(G\), and \(G_0\triangleleft G\) has finite index, then \(P\cap G_0\) generates \(G_0\).
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
The image of \(P\) is the whole finite quotient. Choose coset representatives in \(P\). A Schreier generator, or its inverse, has the form \(rp(r')^{-1}\), with \(r,p,r'\in P\) and \(rpG_0=r'G_0\). Choose \(c\in P\) representing \((r'G_0)^{-1}\). Then
\[
rp(r')^{-1}=(rpc)(r'c)^{-1},\qquad rpc,r'c\in P\cap G_0.
\]
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:compression}
The subgroup \(H_0\) is infranormal and nonnormal in \(\Gamma_0\). With \(E_{ij}\) the matrix units, put
\begin{equation}\label{eq:tr}
t=(I_3,I_3+3E_{12}),\qquad r=(I_3+3x_2E_{12},I_3).
\end{equation}
Then \(t\in\Gamma_0\), \(r\in H_0\), and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:strict}
tH_0t^{-1}\subset H_0,\qquad
t^{-1}rt=(I_3+3x_1^{-3}x_2E_{12},I_3)\notin H_0.
\end{equation}
Moreover \(I=\Gamma_0/H_0\) is countably infinite.
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
The compression monoid of \(H_{\mathbb Z}\) contains \(H_{\mathbb Z}\) and \((I_3,I_3+E_{ij})\), \(i\ne j\). The latter preserve nonnegative exponents and generate the substitution group. For \(v=ku\in\mathbb Z^3\setminus\{0\}\), with \(k\geq1\) and \(u\) primitive, choose \(S\in\operatorname{SL}_3(\mathbb Z)\) with \(Se_1=u\). Then
\[
S\cdot x_1^k=x^v.
\]
Thus substitution conjugates of \(H_{\mathbb Z}\) contain all elementary Laurent monomials and generate \(N_{\mathbb Z}\). Lemma~\ref{lem:monoid}, together with normality of \(\Gamma_0\), proves infranormality of \(H_0\).

The substitution \(t\) sends \(x_2\) to \(x_1^3x_2\) and fixes \(x_1,x_3\), giving \eqref{eq:strict}. The powers \(t^j\) have distinct substitution components, whereas every element of \(H_0\) has trivial substitution component. Hence their cosets are distinct.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
\label{prop:wreath}
The group \(E\) is finitely generated, torsion-free and nonhyperlinear. The nonidentity word
\[
w=[r,tat^{-1}]
\]
is killed by every homomorphism from \(E\) to the unitary group of a tracial matrix ultraproduct. Its kernel \(A\) and quotient \(\Gamma_0\) in the defining split extension are residually finite.
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
By \eqref{eq:strict},
\[
w=a_{rtH_0}a_{tH_0}^{-1}\ne1.
\]
For \(\pi:E\to\mathcal U(\mathcal Q_\omega)\), set \(\mathcal D=\pi(H_0)'\cap\mathcal Q_\omega\). Since \([a,H_0]=1\), Theorem~\ref{thm:normalization} gives
\[
\pi(a)\in \mathcal D,\qquad
\pi(tat^{-1})\in\pi(t)\mathcal D\pi(t)^*=\mathcal D,\qquad
\pi(w)=1.
\]
Thus \(E\) is not hyperlinear. A finite generating set of \(\Gamma_0\), together with \(a\), generates \(E\). Both kernel and quotient are torsion-free, so is \(E\). Finally, coordinate reduction modulo integers separates the elements of \(A\).
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
\label{prop:double}
The group \(\Delta\) is finitely generated, torsion-free and nonhyperlinear. Every matrix-ultraproduct homomorphism kills \(w_\Delta\ne1\). The fold map gives a split exact sequence
\[
1\longrightarrow \mathbb F_\infty\longrightarrow\Delta\longrightarrow\Gamma_0\longrightarrow1.
\]
Its kernel and quotient are residually finite.
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Since \(tH_0t^{-1}\subset H_0\), the amalgam relations give \([a_\Delta,H_0]=1\). Moreover,
\[
w_\Delta=\iota_2(t)\,\iota_1(t^{-1}rt)\,\iota_2(t^{-1}r^{-1})\ne1:
\]
the three syllables lie outside \(H_0\), by \eqref{eq:strict} and their substitution components. Apply \cite[Chapter~I, Section~1.2, Theorem~2]{Serre80}. For \(\pi:\Delta\to\mathcal U(\mathcal Q_\omega)\), set \(\mathcal D=\pi(H_0)'\cap\mathcal Q_\omega\). Theorem~\ref{thm:normalization} gives
\[
\pi(a_\Delta)\in \mathcal D,\qquad
\pi(b_\Delta)=\pi(\iota_1(t))\pi(a_\Delta)\pi(\iota_1(t))^*\in \mathcal D,
\qquad \pi(w_\Delta)=1.
\]

The fold map splits through either vertex. Its kernel acts freely on the Bass--Serre tree; the quotient graph has two vertices and one edge for each element of \(\Gamma_0/H_0\). Thus the kernel is \(\mathbb F_\infty\), hence residually finite. Every torsion element is conjugate into a vertex group, so \(\Delta\) is torsion-free; the two vertices also give finite generation. See \cite[Chapter~I, Theorem~4', Proposition~18 and Theorem~8]{Serre80} for these tree-action facts.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:nonqwep}
Both \(\mathcal L(E)\) and \(\mathcal L(\Delta)\) are non-QWEP, although all four kernels and quotients displayed above are hyperlinear and sofic.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
Apply \eqref{eq:bridge} and residual finiteness of the kernels and quotients.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
\label{thm:hyperfinite}
The group \(\Gamma_0\) admits an outer trace-preserving action on the hyperfinite II$_1$ factor \(\mathcal R_0\) whose crossed product is a non-QWEP II$_1$ factor.
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
Choose a Haar unitary \(z\in \mathcal R_0\), and let \(\mathcal E_0:\mathcal R_0\to B_0=W^*(z)\) be the trace-preserving expectation. Then
\[
\mathcal M\cong\,\overline\otimes\,_{i\in I}B_0\subset
\mathcal R_I=\,\overline\otimes\,_{i\in I}(\mathcal R_0,\tau_0)\cong \mathcal R_0.
\]
The coordinate-permutation action \(\widetilde\beta\) extends \(\beta\), and \(\mathcal E_\mathcal M=\,\overline\otimes\,_I \mathcal E_0\) is equivariant. Hence
\[
\mathcal E_\mathcal M\rtimes\mathrm{Id}:\mathcal R_I\rtimes_{\widetilde\beta}\Gamma_0
\longrightarrow \mathcal M\rtimes_\beta\Gamma_0,\qquad
\sum_gx_g\lambda(g)\longmapsto\sum_g\mathcal E_\mathcal M(x_g)\lambda(g)
\]
is a trace-preserving conditional expectation. Its range is \(\mathcal L(E)\), so the domain is non-QWEP. The following lemma proves outerness and factoriality.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:faithful-outer}
The coset action \(\Gamma_0\curvearrowright I\) is faithful, and its permutation action on \(\mathcal R_I\) is outer. Consequently \(\mathcal R_I\rtimes\Gamma_0\) is a II$_1$ factor.
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
Let \(C=\bigcap_{\gamma\in\Gamma_0}\gamma H_0\gamma^{-1}\). For \((B,I_3)\in C\), normality implies that every entry of \(B\) remains polynomial under
\[
x^v\longmapsto x^{(I_3+3kE_{ij})v},\qquad k\in\mathbb Z,\quad i\ne j.
\]
If a nonconstant monomial \(x^v\) occurs, choose \(v_j\ne0\), \(i\ne j\), and \(k\) with \(v_i+3kv_j<0\). Distinct monomials remain distinct, contradicting polynomiality. Thus \(B\) is constant.

For \(i\ne j\), put \(q_{ij}=I_3+3x_1^{-1}E_{ij}\). Since \((q_{ij},I_3)\in\Gamma_0\),
\[
q_{ij}Bq_{ij}^{-1}
=B+3x_1^{-1}(E_{ij}B-BE_{ij})-9x_1^{-2}E_{ij}BE_{ij}
\]
is polynomial. Hence \([E_{ij},B]=0\) for all \(i\ne j\), so \(B=cI_3\). As \(c\in\mathbb Z\) and \(\det B=1\), we have \(B=I_3\) and \(C=\{1\}\).

Write \(\mathcal R_0=\,\overline\otimes\,_{n\geq1}(\mathbb M_2,\operatorname{tr}_2)\). For \(g\ne e\), choose \(i\in I\) with \(gi\ne i\), and let \(z_n=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)\) in the \(n\)-th matrix factor of coordinate \(i\). Then
\[
\lVert[x,z_n]\rVert_2\longrightarrow0\quad(x\in \mathcal R_I),\qquad
\lVert\widetilde\beta_g(z_n)-z_n\rVert_2^2=2.
\]
Thus \(\widetilde\beta_g\) is outer. If \(\sum_gx_g\lambda(g)\) is central, then
\[
x_g\widetilde\beta_g(y)=yx_g\qquad(y\in \mathcal R_I).
\]
Outerness gives \(x_g=0\) for \(g\ne e\), and \(x_e\in\mathbb C\). The crossed product is therefore a finite diffuse factor.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- proposition-5: body_md -->
\label{prop:necessary}
Let \((\mathcal M,\tau)\) be a finite von Neumann algebra with faithful normal tracial state, and let \(G\) act preserving \(\tau\). If \(\mathcal M\rtimes G\) is QWEP, then both \(\mathcal M\) and \(\mathcal L(G)\) are QWEP.
<!-- end proposition-5 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
The canonical trace gives conditional expectations onto \(\mathcal M\) and \(\mathcal L(G)\), respectively:
\[
\sum_gx_g\lambda(g)\longmapsto x_e,
\qquad
\sum_gx_g\lambda(g)\longmapsto\sum_g\tau(x_g)\lambda(g).
\]
Apply QWEP permanence under conditional expectations.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- theorem-7: body_md -->
\label{thm:mixed}
Both \(\mathcal M\) and \(\mathcal L(G)\) are QWEP, whereas
\[
\mathcal R_\sigma=\mathcal M\rtimes_{\beta,\sigma}G
\]
is non-QWEP. The scalar cocycle \(\sigma\) cannot be removed by a cochain with values in \(\mathcal U(\mathcal M)\).
<!-- end theorem-7 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
The first assertion follows from commutativity of \(\mathcal M\) and residual finiteness of \(G\). Since \(\sigma|_{\Gamma_0\times\Gamma_0}=1\), there is a trace-preserving expected inclusion
\[
\mathcal L(E)\cong \mathcal M\rtimes\Gamma_0\subset \mathcal R_\sigma.
\]
Hence \(\mathcal R_\sigma\) is non-QWEP.

Put \(U_g=\lambda_\sigma(g,0)\) and \(V=\lambda_\sigma(e,1)\). Then \(U_gV=\chi(g)VU_g\). If \((b_x)_{x\in G}\subset\mathcal U(\mathcal M)\) removed the cocycle, the corrected implementers for $(g,0)$ and $(e,1)$ would commute. Since \(\mathcal M\) is abelian and \(\mathbb Z\) acts trivially,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:eigenunitary}
\beta_g(b_{(e,1)})=\chi(g)^{-1}b_{(e,1)}.
\end{equation}
Write \(b_{(e,1)}=\sum_{a\in A}c_a\lambda(a)\) in \(L_2(\mathcal M)\). Then
\[
|c_{ga}|=|c_a|,\qquad \sum_{a\in A}|c_a|^2<\infty.
\]
Every \(a\ne0\) has infinite orbit: otherwise the union of its orbit supports would be a finite nonempty invariant subset of the infinite transitive set \(I\). Thus \(c_a=0\) for \(a\ne0\). Equation~\eqref{eq:eigenunitary} now contradicts \(\chi(t)\ne1\).
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- proposition-6: body_md -->
\label{prop:scalar}
There is a trace-preserving isomorphism
\[
\mathcal M\rtimes_{\beta,\sigma_\theta}Q
\cong\mathcal L(E)\,\overline\otimes\,\mathcal L_{\sigma_\theta}(\mathbb Z^2).
\]
This crossed product is non-QWEP. Moreover \(\sigma_\theta\) is not a coboundary for this action with values in \(\mathcal U(\mathcal M)\).
<!-- end proposition-6 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
The two commuting families \(\mathcal M,\{\lambda_{\sigma_\theta}(g,0,0)\}\) and \(\{\lambda_{\sigma_\theta}(e,m,n)\}\) generate the respective tensor factors, and their canonical traces multiply. This gives the isomorphism. Applying \(\mathrm{Id}\,\overline\otimes\,\tau_{\sigma_\theta}\) yields the non-QWEP expected subalgebra \(\mathcal L(E)\).

On \(\{e\}\times\mathbb Z^2\), the action is trivial and \(\mathcal M\) is abelian. Every \(\mathcal U(\mathcal M)\)-valued coboundary \(b_sb_tb_{s+t}^*\) is therefore symmetric. In contrast,
\[
\sigma_\theta(e_2,e_1)=e^{2\pi i\theta}\ne1=\sigma_\theta(e_1,e_2).
\]
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- proposition-7: body_md -->
\label{prop:diagonal}
Let $\alpha:G\curvearrowright \mathcal M$ be an action and let $\sigma\in Z^2(G,\mathbb T)$. Put $\mathcal R_1=\mathcal M\rtimes_\alpha G$ and $\mathcal R_\sigma=\mathcal M\rtimes_{\alpha,\sigma}G$. There are faithful normal embeddings with normal conditional expectations
\[
\mathcal R_\sigma\hookrightarrow \mathcal R_1\,\overline\otimes\,\mathcal L_\sigma(G),
\qquad
\mathcal R_1\hookrightarrow \mathcal R_\sigma\,\overline\otimes\,\mathcal L_{\bar\sigma}(G).
\]
Consequently, if $\mathcal L_\sigma(G)$ is QWEP, then $\mathcal R_\sigma$ is QWEP if and only if $\mathcal R_1$ is QWEP.
<!-- end proposition-7 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
Write $\lambda(g)$ and $\lambda_\sigma(g)$ for the canonical unitaries. The maps
\[
x\lambda_\sigma(g)\longmapsto x\lambda(g)\otimes\lambda_\sigma(g),\qquad
x\lambda(g)\longmapsto x\lambda_\sigma(g)\otimes\lambda_{\bar\sigma}(g)
\]
preserve the crossed-product relations. In the regular representations,
their ranges are the crossed products associated with
$\Delta G\subset G\times G$. The subgroup expectations satisfy
\[
\mathcal E_{\Delta G}(x\lambda(g)\otimes\lambda_\sigma(h))
=\delta_{g,h}\,x\lambda(g)\otimes\lambda_\sigma(h),
\]
and similarly for the second map. Since
$\mathcal L_{\bar\sigma}(G)\cong\mathcal L_\sigma(G)^{\rm op}$, tensor-product and
expectation permanence give the conclusion.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- theorem-8: body_md -->
\label{thm:scalarfactorization}
Let $\alpha:G\curvearrowright \mathcal M$ admit an invariant normal state $\varphi$, and let $\sigma\in Z^2(G,\mathbb T)$. Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:scalarfactorization}
\mathcal M\rtimes_{\alpha,\sigma}G\text{ is QWEP}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\mathcal M\rtimes_\alpha G\text{ and }\mathcal L_\sigma(G)\text{ are QWEP}.
\end{equation}
In particular, this holds for every finite trace-preserving action.
<!-- end theorem-8 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
Invariance of $\varphi$ gives the normal conditional expectation
\[
\mathcal E_\varphi:\mathcal M\rtimes_{\alpha,\sigma}G\longrightarrow\mathcal L_\sigma(G),
\qquad \mathcal E_\varphi(x\lambda_\sigma(g))=\varphi(x)\lambda_\sigma(g).
\]
Indeed, apply $\varphi$ to the coefficient entries in the regular
representation. Thus QWEP of the crossed product implies QWEP of
$\mathcal L_\sigma(G)$. Both directions now follow from
Proposition~\ref{prop:diagonal}.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
\label{cor:allscalartwists}
If a finite trace-preserving action has a non-QWEP ordinary crossed product, all its scalar-twisted crossed products are non-QWEP. In particular, this holds for each action in Theorem~\ref{thm:overview}\textup{(i)}.
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:scalarfactorization}.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:scalar}
If $\mathcal L_\sigma(G)$ is QWEP, then $\mathcal L(G)$ is QWEP. Consequently, QWEP of a finite trace-preserving scalar-twisted crossed product implies QWEP of both its coefficient algebra and $\mathcal L(G)$.
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
The diagonal map
\[
\lambda(g)\longmapsto\lambda_\sigma(g)\otimes\lambda_{\bar\sigma}(g)
\]
embeds $\mathcal L(G)$ trace-preservingly into $\mathcal L_\sigma(G)\,\overline\otimes\,\mathcal L_{\bar\sigma}(G)$. The two factors are QWEP simultaneously, and the image is expected. For the crossed-product assertion, use the coefficient expectation and the expectation onto $\mathcal L_\sigma(G)$. This is the scalar cancellation argument in \cite[Proposition 3.1.20]{Zeng23}.
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- corollary-3: body_md -->
\label{cor:CHactions}
For a hyperlinear group $G$, the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2em]
\item $G$ is cocycle-hyperlinear;
\item every finite trace-preserving action of $G$ with QWEP ordinary crossed product has QWEP scalar-twisted crossed products.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end corollary-3 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
The first implication follows from Theorem~\ref{thm:scalarfactorization}. For the converse, apply \textup{(ii)} to the trivial action on $\mathbb C$.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
For an arbitrary action, Proposition~\ref{prop:diagonal} still gives
\[
\mathcal M\rtimes_\alpha G\text{ QWEP},\quad
\mathcal M\rtimes_{\alpha,\sigma}G\text{ non-QWEP}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \mathcal L_\sigma(G)\text{ non-QWEP}.
\]
An invariant semifinite trace does not suffice for Theorem~\ref{thm:scalarfactorization}; see Proposition~\ref{prop:translation}.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- proposition-8: body_md -->
\label{prop:typeIdecomp}
Choose \(u(e)=1\) and \(u(g)\in\mathcal U(K)\) with \(\beta_g=\operatorname{Ad}_{u(g)}\). There is a normalized scalar \(2\)-cocycle \(\sigma\) such that
\[
u(g)u(h)=\sigma(g,h)u(gh).
\]
Its cohomology class in \(H^2(G,\mathbb T)\) is independent of these choices. The action is implemented by a genuine unitary representation on \(K\) if and only if \([\sigma]=0\). Moreover,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:typeIdecomp}
B(K)\rtimes_\beta G\ \cong\ B(K)\,\overline\otimes\,\mathcal L_{\bar\sigma}(G).
\end{equation}
Consequently this crossed product is QWEP if and only if \(\mathcal L_{\bar\sigma}(G)\) is QWEP.
<!-- end proposition-8 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
Since $\operatorname{Ad}_{u(g)u(h)u(gh)^*}=\mathrm{Id}$, there is $\sigma(g,h)\in\mathbb T$ with $u(g)u(h)=\sigma(g,h)u(gh)$. 

Associativity gives the cocycle identity, Any other normalized choice of implementing unitaries has the form \(u'(g)=b_gu(g)\), where \(b_g\in\mathbb T\) and \(b_e=1\). The corresponding cocycle is
\[
\sigma'(g,h)=b_gb_h\overline{b_{gh}}\,\sigma(g,h),
\]
so \(\sigma'\) and \(\sigma\) differ by a scalar coboundary and define the same class in \(H^2(G,\mathbb T)\).
This proves the lifting criterion.

For the canonical crossed-product unitaries $\lambda(g)$, put $w(g)=u(g)^*\lambda(g)$.
Then
\[
[w(g),x]=0\quad(x\in B(K)),\qquad
w(g)w(h)=\overline{\sigma(g,h)}w(gh).
\]
In the regular representation on $\ell_2(G,K)$, let
$(D\xi)(t)=u(t^{-1})^*\xi(t)$. Then
\[
D\pi_\beta(x)D^*=1\otimes x,\qquad
D\lambda(g)D^*=\lambda_{\bar\sigma}(g)\otimes u(g).
\]
This proves \eqref{eq:typeIdecomp}. Since $B(K)$ is injective,
tensor permanence and a normal-state slice give the QWEP equivalence.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
\label{rem:pauli}

In this remark we construct a finite action which can not be lifted.

Let \(G=(\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)^2\), \(K=\mathbb C^2\), and
\[
U=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad
V=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad UV=-VU.
\]
The action $\beta_{(a,b)}=\operatorname{Ad}_{U^aV^b}$ has multiplier
\[
\sigma((a,b),(c,d))=(-1)^{bc}.
\]
Every implementing pair is a scalar multiple of $U,V$, so $\beta$ does not lift. The four monomials $U^aV^b$ form a basis of $\mathbb M_2$; hence
\[
\mathbb M_2\rtimes_\beta G\cong \mathbb M_4,
\qquad
\mathbb M_2\,\overline\otimes\,\mathcal L(G)\cong\bigoplus_{j=1}^{4}\mathbb M_2.
\]
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- proposition-9: body_md -->
\label{prop:projectivecriterion}
Assume \(G\) is hyperlinear, and retain the multiplier \(\sigma\) from Proposition~\ref{prop:typeIdecomp}. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2em]
\item \(B(K)\rtimes_\beta G\) is QWEP.
\item There are dimensions \(d_n\) and maps \(r_n:G\to\mathcal U(\mathbb M_{d_n})\), with \(r_n(e)=1\), such that for every \(g,h\in G\),
\begin{equation}\label{eq:projectiveapprox}
\lim_{n\to\infty}
\bigl\|r_n(g)r_n(h)-\sigma(g,h)r_n(gh)\bigr\|_{2,d_n}=0.
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
No trace-separation condition is imposed on the maps \(r_n\).
<!-- end proposition-9 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
If \textup{(i)} holds, $\mathcal L_\sigma(G)$ is Connes embeddable.
Unitary microstates and a diagonal choice over $G$ give \textup{(ii)}.

Conversely, put
\[
r(g)=[r_n(g)]_\omega,\qquad \mathcal P=\{r(g):g\in G\}'',\qquad
W_g=\lambda(g)\otimes\overline{r(g)}\in\mathcal L(G)\,\overline\otimes\,\overline \mathcal P.
\]
Both tensor factors are QWEP, and
\[
W_gW_h=\bar\sigma(g,h)W_{gh},\qquad
(\tau_G\otimes\bar\tau_\mathcal P)(W_g)=\delta_{g,e}.
\]
Hence $\{W_g:g\in G\}''\cong\mathcal L_{\bar\sigma}(G)$ trace-preservingly.
The trace-preserving expectation and Proposition~\ref{prop:typeIdecomp}
give \textup{(i)}.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- corollary-4: body_md -->
\label{cor:typeIpositive}
For hyperlinear \(G\), the crossed product \(B(K)\rtimes_\beta G\) is QWEP in each of the following cases:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2em]
\item \([\sigma]=0\), equivalently \(\beta\) has a genuine implementing representation;
\item \(\sigma\) has a finite-dimensional projective unitary realization, possibly on a space different from \(K\);
\item \(\beta\) admits an invariant state on \(B(K)\), not necessarily a normal state.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, the answer is positive whenever \(K\) is finite-dimensional.
<!-- end corollary-4 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
Cases \textup{(i)} and \textup{(ii)} follow from
Proposition~\ref{prop:projectivecriterion} with exact projective models.
For \textup{(iii)}, put $\mathcal D=C^*(u(g):g\in G)$. Invariance gives
\[
\varphi(u(g)x)=\varphi(xu(g))\qquad(x\in B(K),\ g\in G).
\]
Thus $\varphi|_\mathcal D$ is an amenable trace. By
\cite[Theorem~6.1, \textup{(i)}$\Rightarrow$\textup{(ii')}]{Ozawa04},
there is a unital $*$-homomorphism $\theta:\mathcal D\to \mathcal R_0^\omega$.
Since
\[
\theta(u(g))\theta(u(h))=\sigma(g,h)\theta(u(gh)),
\]
the tensor argument in Proposition~\ref{prop:projectivecriterion} applies.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- corollary-5: body_md -->
\label{cor:CFtypeI}
If \(G\) is cocycle-hyperlinear, then \(B(K)\rtimes_\beta G\) is QWEP for every action \(\beta\) and every nonzero Hilbert space \(K\). This applies to amenable-by-treeable groups, to
\[
\operatorname{SL}_n(\mathbb Z),\quad \operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb Z),\quad
\operatorname{PSL}_n(\mathbb Z)\qquad(n\geq2),
\]
and to their countable central extensions.
<!-- end corollary-5 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
Combine Proposition~\ref{prop:typeIdecomp} with
\cite[Theorem~A, Theorem~4.4 and Corollary~4.5]{CF26}.
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- proposition-10: body_md -->
\label{prop:laurent-inflation}
Let $R=\mathbb F_{11}[t,t^{-1}]$ and $Q=\operatorname{SL}_3(R)$. Then $Q$ is residually finite and $H^2(Q,\mathbb T)\cong C_{10}$. If $[\sigma]\ne0$, then the full twisted group $C^*$-algebra $C^*_\sigma(Q)$ has no nonzero finite-dimensional representation, and $[\sigma]$ is not inflated from a finite quotient.
<!-- end proposition-10 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
By \cite[Theorem~5]{Sug21} and \cite[Lemma~6.4]{KLPV25}, the universal central extension is
\[
1\longrightarrow C_{10}\longrightarrow
U=\operatorname{St}_3(R)\longrightarrow Q\longrightarrow1.
\]
Thus $H^2(Q,\mathbb T)\cong\widehat{C_{10}}$. Finite-ring reductions give residual finiteness.

For $\pi:U\to\mathcal U(\mathbb M_n)$, the root-subgroup images are finite abelian of exponent $11$. Weyl conjugation and the Steinberg relations make their common kernel a finite-index ideal $I\lhd R$. Hence $\pi$ factors through $\operatorname{St}_3(B)$, $B=R/I$. By \cite[Lemma~17 and its proof]{KS09}, $K_{2,3}(B)=K_2(B)$. In each local factor, unit symbols generate $K_2$ and are bimultiplicative \cite[\S3, Theorem~3.2]{KN06}. Coefficient-field symbols vanish \cite[Lemma~6.1\textup{(1)}]{KLPV25}, and principal units have $11$-power order. Thus $K_2(B)$ is $11$-primary, so $\pi$ kills $C_{10}$.

A finite-dimensional $\sigma$-projective representation lifts to $U$ with central character $[\sigma]$, which must be trivial. An inflated class would admit such a representation by the twisted regular representation of the finite quotient.
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- example-1: body_md -->
\label{ex:fd-gap-qwep}
Let
\[
P=\mathbb Z[1/5]^2\rtimes\mathbb Z,\qquad
(a,b,k)(a',b',k')=(a+a'+kb',b+b',k+k').
\]
By \cite[Definition~2.2 and Lemma~2.3]{Eckhardt25}, $P$ is amenable and residually finite. Thus $B=C^*(P)$ is nuclear and residually finite-dimensional, since its finite-quotient traces converge to the faithful canonical trace.

Put $b_0=(0,1,0)$, $g_0=(1/5,0,0)$ and $\zeta=e^{2\pi i/5}$. The normal closure of $b_0$ is $H=\mathbb Z^2$, since $[(0,0,1),b_0]=(1,0,0)$. In $E=P/H$, $z=g_0H$ is central of order $5$. For $G=E/\langle z\rangle$, the character $z\mapsto\zeta$ defines $\sigma$ with
\[
C^*_\sigma(G)\cong B/I,\qquad
I=\overline{\langle u_{b_0}-1,u_{g_0}-\zeta1\rangle}.
\]
Here $I$ is the closed two-sided ideal, and $\mathcal L_\sigma(G)$ is injective since $G$ is amenable.

In any irreducible finite-dimensional representation $\rho$ of $P$, the first coordinate acts by a character $\chi$ of finite order prime to $5$ \cite[Lemmas~2.1 and~2.7]{Eckhardt25}. If $\chi(1)=1$, then $\rho(g_0)=I$; otherwise $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(b_0))=0$. Since $|1-\zeta|^2<2$, every unital $\pi:B\to\mathbb M_n$ satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fd-gap-injective}
\|\pi(u_{b_0})-I_n\|_{2,n}^2+
\|\pi(u_{g_0})-\zeta I_n\|_{2,n}^2
\geq |1-\zeta|^2>0,
\end{equation}
where $\|x\|_{2,n}^2=\operatorname{tr}_n(x^*x)$. Hence $C^*_\sigma(G)$ has no nonzero finite-dimensional representation and $[\sigma]\ne0$.
<!-- end example-1 -->
<!-- theorem-9: body_md -->
\label{thm:twistedregularwreath}
Let \(A,\Gamma\) be countable groups, with \(\Gamma\) residually finite, and put \(W=A^{(\Gamma)}\rtimes\Gamma=A\wr\Gamma\). Identify \(A\) with its identity-coordinate copy \(A_e\). For a normalized scalar cocycle \(\sigma\) on \(W\), put \(\alpha=\sigma|_{A_e\times A_e}\) and \(\eta=\sigma|_{\Gamma\times\Gamma}\). Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:wreathcriterion}
\mathcal L_\sigma(W)\text{ is QWEP}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\mathcal L_\alpha(A)\text{ and }\mathcal L_\eta(\Gamma)\text{ are QWEP}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-9 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
Necessity follows from the expected subgroup inclusions. Conversely, let \(\pi:W\to\Gamma\) be the quotient, and put
\[
\rho(w,z)=\sigma(w,z)\overline{\eta(\pi(w),\pi(z))}.
\]
Then \(\rho|_\Gamma=1\) and \(\rho|_{A_e}=\alpha\). In \(\mathcal L_\rho(W)\), let \(V(g)\) and \(U_e(a)\) be the canonical unitaries associated with \(\Gamma\) and \(A_e\), respectively. Put \(U_s(a)=V(s)U_e(a)V(s)^*\). We have
\begin{align}
U_s(a)U_s(b)&=\alpha(a,b)U_s(ab),\label{eq:lampwithin}\\
V(g)U_s(a)V(g)^*&=U_{gs}(a).\label{eq:lampcovariance}
\end{align}
For \(s\ne t\), the scalar commutator of \(U_s(a),U_t(b)\) is multiplicative in each variable. Thus it factors through \(B=A_{\mathrm{ab}}\); covariance gives bicharacters \(\kappa_r:B\times B\to\mathbb T\), \(r\ne e\), with
\begin{align}
U_s(a)U_t(b)&=\kappa_{s^{-1}t}(\bar a,\bar b)U_t(b)U_s(a),\label{eq:lampcross}\\
\kappa_{r^{-1}}(y,x)&=\overline{\kappa_r(x,y)}.\label{eq:lampsymmetry}
\end{align}

Fix finitely many words, including adjoints. Move their group letters to the right using \eqref{eq:lampcovariance}, and let \(S,T\subset\Gamma\) be the resulting coordinate indices and terminal group labels. Choose a finite quotient \(q:\Gamma\to Q\) injective on \(\{e\}\cup S\cup S^{-1}S\), with \(q(t)\ne e\) for \(t\in T\setminus\{e\}\). Define bicharacters on \(Q\setminus\{e\}\) by
\[
\kappa^Q_{q(s^{-1}t)}=\kappa_{s^{-1}t}\quad(s,t\in S,\ s\ne t),
\qquad
\kappa^Q_{r^{-1}}(y,x)=\overline{\kappa^Q_r(x,y)},
\]
and use the trivial bicharacter on the remaining inverse pairs. This is consistent: \(q\) separates the inverse-closed difference set, and actual involutions already satisfy \eqref{eq:lampsymmetry}.

Order \(Q=\{q_1,\ldots,q_m\}\), and define
\[
\chi_Q(x,y)=\prod_{i>j}\kappa^Q_{q_i^{-1}q_j}(x_i,y_j)
\qquad(x,y\in B^Q),
\]
\[
c_Q(a,b)=\left(\prod_{i=1}^m\alpha(a_i,b_i)\right)\chi_Q(\bar a,\bar b),
\qquad \mathcal M_Q=\mathcal L_{c_Q}(A^Q).
\]
The bicharacter \(\chi_Q\) is a cocycle. The coordinate generators of \(\mathcal M_Q\) satisfy \eqref{eq:lampwithin} and \eqref{eq:lampcross} with \(\kappa^Q\): the factors in \(\chi_Q\) arise from ordering the product of two coordinate monomials. Moreover,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-lamp-embedding}
\mathcal M_Q\longrightarrow
\left(\,\overline\otimes\,_{i=1}^m\mathcal L_\alpha(A)\right)\,\overline\otimes\,\mathcal L_{\chi_Q}(B^Q)
\end{equation}
is the trace-preserving embedding given by
\[
\lambda_{c_Q}(a)\longmapsto
\left(\bigotimes_{i=1}^m\lambda_\alpha(a_i)\right)\otimes\lambda_{\chi_Q}(\bar a).
\]
Its first factor supplies trace zero for \(a\ne e\). Since \(B^Q\) is abelian, \(\mathcal L_{\chi_Q}(B^Q)\) is injective; hence \(\mathcal M_Q\) is Connes embeddable.

The assignments \(U_s(a)\mapsto U_{rs}(a)\), \(r,s\in Q\), preserve the coordinate relations, because
\[
(rs)^{-1}(rt)=s^{-1}t.
\]
Ordered monomials form a basis indexed by \(A^Q\), so these assignments define a genuine trace-preserving action of \(Q\) on \(\mathcal M_Q\). Its crossed product satisfies
\[
\mathcal P_Q=\mathcal M_Q\rtimes Q\hookrightarrow \mathbb M_{|Q|}\,\overline\otimes\, \mathcal M_Q
\]
trace-preservingly, and is therefore Connes embeddable.

Replace \(U_s(a),V(g)\) in the chosen words by the corresponding \(q(s)\)-coordinate and \(q(g)\)-unitaries in \(\mathcal P_Q\). Their traces agree: nonidentity terminal labels and nontrivial coordinate configurations remain nontrivial, while words reducing to the identity retain all \(\alpha\)-, \(\kappa\)- and inverse phases. Approximating these finite collections of moments by matrices proves that \(\mathcal L_\rho(W)\) is Connes embeddable. Finally,
\[
\mathcal L_\sigma(W)\hookrightarrow\mathcal L_\rho(W)\,\overline\otimes\,\mathcal L_\eta(\Gamma),
\qquad
\lambda_\sigma(w)\longmapsto\lambda_\rho(w)\otimes\lambda_\eta(\pi(w))
\]
is trace-preserving, since \(\rho\,\pi^*\eta=\sigma\). This proves sufficiency.
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- corollary-6: body_md -->
\label{cor:CHwreath}
For countable \(A\) and residually finite \(\Gamma\),
\[
A\wr\Gamma\text{ is cocycle-hyperlinear}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
A\text{ and }\Gamma\text{ are cocycle-hyperlinear}.
\]
For amenable \(A\), criterion \eqref{eq:wreathcriterion} reduces to the restriction to \(\Gamma\). In particular, \(\mathbb Z\wr\Gamma\) is cocycle-hyperlinear exactly when \(\Gamma\) is cocycle-hyperlinear.
<!-- end corollary-6 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
Sufficiency follows from Theorem~\ref{thm:twistedregularwreath}. Conversely, every cocycle on \(\Gamma\) inflates to \(W\). For \(\alpha\in Z^2(A,\mathbb T)\), put
\[
c(a,b)=\prod_{s\in\Gamma}\alpha(a_s,b_s),\qquad
\widetilde c((a,g),(b,h))=c(a,g\cdot b).
\]
The finite product \(c\) is shift-invariant, so \(\widetilde c\) is a cocycle on \(W\) restricting to \(\alpha\) on \(A_e\). Expected subgroup inclusions give necessity. If \(A\) is amenable, all its scalar-twisted group algebras are injective.
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- remark-3: body_md -->
\label{rem:augmentation}
Let \(W=\mathbb Z^{(\Gamma)}\rtimes\Gamma\), \(I_\Gamma=\ker(\sum:\mathbb Z^{(\Gamma)}\to\mathbb Z)\), and \(H=I_\Gamma\rtimes\Gamma\). For \(\rho\in Z^2(\Gamma,\mathbb T)\), put
\[
\Omega_\rho((a,g),(b,h))=\prod_{t\in\Gamma}\rho(g,t)^{b_t}.
\]
The cocycle identity follows from that of $\rho$ and $\sum_t a_t=0$. Its restrictions along
\[
g\longmapsto(0,g),\qquad g\longmapsto(\delta_g-\delta_e,g)
\]
are $1$ and $\rho$. These embeddings are conjugate by $(-\delta_e,e)\in W$, so extension of $[\Omega_\rho]$ to $W$ forces $[\rho]=0$. Conversely, if $\rho=\delta c$, then $\Omega_\rho=\delta F$ for $F(a,g)=\prod_t c(t)^{a_t}$. Thus $[\Omega_\rho]$ extends to $W$ exactly when $[\rho]=0$.
<!-- end remark-3 -->
<!-- proposition-11: body_md -->
\label{prop:fourier-qwep}
Let $1<p<\infty$. If $\mathcal R$ is QWEP, then
\[
\mathsf M_{\mathrm{cb}}(L_p(\mathcal L(G)))
\subset\mathsf M_{\mathrm{cb}}(L_p(\mathcal R))\quad\text{contractively}.
\]
<!-- end proposition-11 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
The trace-preserving embedding
\[
\Phi:\mathcal R\longrightarrow\mathcal R\,\overline\otimes\,\mathcal L(G),\qquad
\Phi(a\lambda_\sigma(s))=a\lambda_\sigma(s)\otimes\lambda(s)
\]
induces a complete isometry on $L_p$. Write $\widetilde T_\varphi$
for the Fourier multiplier on $L_p(\mathcal L(G))$. Then
\[
\Phi T_\varphi=(\mathrm{Id}\otimes\widetilde T_\varphi)\Phi,
\qquad
\|T_\varphi\|_{\mathrm{cb}}
\le\|\mathrm{Id}\otimes\widetilde T_\varphi\|_{\mathrm{cb}}
=\|\widetilde T_\varphi\|_{\mathrm{cb}}.
\]
The last equality uses the tensor-extension principle recalled in
\cite[p.~3 and the proof of Theorem~3.2.2]{Zeng23}; its ultraproduct
construction is given in \cite[Theorem~3.11 and Corollary~3.12]{Junge04}.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- corollary-7: body_md -->
\label{cor:scalar-fourier-qwep}
Let $\sigma\in Z^2(G,\mathbb T)$ and $1<p<\infty$. If $\mathcal L_\sigma(G)$ is QWEP, then
\[
\mathsf M_{\mathrm{cb}}(L_p(\mathcal L_\sigma(G)))
=\mathsf M_{\mathrm{cb}}(L_p(\mathcal L(G)))\quad\text{isometrically}.
\]
<!-- end corollary-7 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
One inclusion follows from Proposition~\ref{prop:fourier-qwep}.
For the converse, $\mathcal L_{\bar\sigma}(G)$ is QWEP and
\[
\lambda(s)\longmapsto
\lambda_{\bar\sigma}(s)\otimes\lambda_\sigma(s)
\]
is a trace-preserving embedding. Apply the same tensor-extension
argument to $\mathrm{Id}\otimes T_\varphi$.
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{lem:amenable-supported-symbols}
Let $H\leq G$ be amenable, $\sigma\in Z^2(G,\mathbb T)$ and $1<p<\infty$.
If $\varphi\in\ell_\infty(G)$ is supported on $H$, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:amenable-supported-symbols}
\|\varphi\|_{\mathsf M_{\mathrm{cb}}(L_p(\mathcal L_\sigma(G)))}
=\|\varphi\|_{\mathsf M_{\mathrm{cb}}(L_p(\mathcal L(G)))}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
Subgroup inclusions and expectations reduce both norms to $H$. Apply Corollary~\ref{cor:scalar-fourier-qwep}, since $\mathcal L_{\sigma|_H}(H)$ is injective.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- corollary-8: body_md -->
\label{cor:multiplier-obstruction}
If, for some $1<p<\infty$ and $\varphi\in\ell_\infty(G)$,
\[
\|\varphi\|_{\mathsf M_{\mathrm{cb}}(L_p(\mathcal L(G)))}
<\|\varphi\|_{\mathsf M_{\mathrm{cb}}(L_p(\mathcal R))},\qquad
\|\varphi\|_{\mathsf M_{\mathrm{cb}}(L_p(\mathcal L(G)))}<\infty,
\]
then $\mathcal R$ is not QWEP.
<!-- end corollary-8 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
Apply Proposition~\ref{prop:fourier-qwep}.
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- proposition-12: body_md -->
\label{prop:fourier-schur}
Let $1<p<\infty$. Then
\[
\|\widetilde\varphi\|_{\mathsf S_{\mathrm{cb}}(S_p(\ell_2(G)))}
\le\|\widetilde\varphi\|_{\mathsf S_{\mathrm{cb}}(L_p(\mathcal N))}
\le\|\varphi\|_{\mathsf M_{\mathrm{cb}}(L_p(\mathcal R))}.
\]
If $\alpha$ is amenable, the second inequality is an equality.
If additionally $\mathcal M$ is QWEP, all three norms are equal.
<!-- end proposition-12 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
The first inequality follows by restriction. For finite $F\subset G$, put
\[
D_F=\sum_{s\in F}\lambda_\sigma(s)\otimes e_{s,s},\qquad
a=\sum_{s,t\in F}a_{s,t}\otimes e_{s,t},\quad a_{s,t}\in\mathcal M.
\]
Since $(D_FaD_F^*)_{s,t}\in\mathcal M\lambda_\sigma(st^{-1})$,
\[
(T_\varphi\otimes\mathrm{Id})(D_FaD_F^*)
=D_F(\mathrm{Id}\otimes M_{\widetilde\varphi})(a)D_F^*.
\]
Taking $L_p$-norms and matrix amplifications proves the second inequality.

If $\alpha$ is amenable, the completely contractive maps in
\cite[Lemmas~3.1.14\textup{(ii)} and~3.1.16]{Zeng23} satisfy
\[
\Phi_{p,i}:L_p(\mathcal R)\longrightarrow L_p(\mathcal N),\qquad
\Psi_{p,i}:L_p(\mathcal N)\longrightarrow L_p(\mathcal R),
\]
\[
\Psi_{p,i}\Phi_{p,i}(x)\longrightarrow x,\qquad
\Phi_{p,i}T_\varphi=(\mathrm{Id}\otimes M_{\widetilde\varphi})\Phi_{p,i}.
\]
Hence $\|T_\varphi\|_{\mathrm{cb}}\le
\|\mathrm{Id}\otimes M_{\widetilde\varphi}\|_{\mathrm{cb}}$.
If $\mathcal M$ is QWEP, tensor extension gives
$\|\mathrm{Id}\otimes M_{\widetilde\varphi}\|_{\mathrm{cb}}
=\|M_{\widetilde\varphi}\|_{\mathrm{cb}}$.
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- problem-1: body_md -->
\label{separation}
Find a hyperlinear group $G$, $\sigma\in Z^2(G,\mathbb T)$,
$1<p<\infty$, $p\ne2$, and $\varphi\in\ell_\infty(G)$ such that
\[
\|\varphi\|_{\mathsf M_{\mathrm{cb}}(L_p(\mathcal L(G)))}
<\|\varphi\|_{\mathsf M_{\mathrm{cb}}(L_p(\mathcal L_\sigma(G)))},\qquad
\|\varphi\|_{\mathsf M_{\mathrm{cb}}(L_p(\mathcal L(G)))}<\infty.
\]
<!-- end problem-1 -->
<!-- proposition-13: body_md -->
\label{prop:coefficientnorm}
Let $n\geq2$, $\zeta=e^{2\pi i/n}$, $G_n=(\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z)^2$, and put $Ue_k=\zeta^ke_k$, $Ve_k=e_{k+1}$ on $\mathbb C^n$. The cocycle $\sigma_n((a,b),(c,d))=\zeta^{-bc}$ identifies $\mathcal L_{\sigma_n}(G_n)$ with $(\mathbb M_n,\operatorname{tr}_n)$. With uniform probability measure on $G_n$, the coefficient map
\[
T_n(U^aV^b)(j,k)=\zeta^{aj+bk}
\]
satisfies, for $1\leq p\leq\infty$,
\[
\|T_n\|_{L_p(\mathbb M_n)\to L_p(G_n)}
=\|T_n^{-1}\|_{L_p(G_n)\to L_p(\mathbb M_n)}
=n^{|1/2-1/p|}.
\]
<!-- end proposition-13 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
For the unitary Fourier matrix $F_{lk}=n^{-1/2}\zeta^{-lk}$,
\[
(T_nx)(j,k)=\sqrt n\,\zeta^{jk}(xF)_{jk},\qquad
(T_n^{-1}f)F=n^{-1/2}[\zeta^{-jk}f(j,k)]_{j,k}.
\]
Both maps are $L_2$-isometries and have $L_\infty$-norm at most $\sqrt n$. Interpolation gives the upper bounds for $p\geq2$.
For $xF=E_{00}$ and $f(j,k)=\zeta^{jk}$,
\[
\frac{\|T_nx\|_p}{\|x\|_p}
=\frac{\|T_n^{-1}f\|_p}{\|f\|_p}=n^{1/2-1/p}.
\]
Since $T_n^*=T_n^{-1}$, duality gives $p\leq2$.
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- theorem-10: body_md -->
\label{thm:reverse}
Let \(G\) be finitely generated and nonhyperlinear. Choose a surjection
\[
p:\mathbb F_d\twoheadrightarrow G,\qquad K=\ker p,
\]
from a free group of finite rank, and a set-theoretic section \(s:G\to \mathbb F_d\) with \(s(e)=e\). On \(\mathcal P=\mathcal L(K)\), define
\begin{align}\label{eq:sectioncocycle}
\alpha_g(\lambda(k))&=\lambda(s(g)ks(g)^{-1}),\\
\sigma(g,h)&=\lambda(s(g)s(h)s(gh)^{-1}).\nonumber
\end{align}
Then \((\alpha,\sigma)\) is a trace-preserving cocycle action and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:freecrossed}
\mathcal P\rtimes_{\alpha,\sigma}G\cong\mathcal L(\mathbb F_d).
\end{equation}
Both \(\mathcal P\) and this crossed product are QWEP, while \(\mathcal L(G)\) is not. No perturbation by unitaries in \(\mathcal P\) can make the cocycle scalar-valued.
<!-- end theorem-10 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
Put $c(g,h)=s(g)s(h)s(gh)^{-1}\in K$. Then
\[
c(g,h)c(gh,k)=s(g)c(h,k)s(g)^{-1}c(g,hk),
\]
which gives the cocycle identities in \eqref{eq:sectioncocycle}.
The map
\[
\sum_g x_g\lambda_\sigma(g)\longmapsto\sum_g x_g\lambda(s(g))
\]
is multiplicative and trace-preserving. Since
$\mathbb F_d=\bigsqcup_{g\in G}Ks(g)$, its image generates $\mathcal L(\mathbb F_d)$.
It therefore extends to \eqref{eq:freecrossed}.

The groups $K$ and $\mathbb F_d$ are free, hence residually finite. Thus $\mathcal P$
and $\mathcal L(\mathbb F_d)$ are QWEP, whereas $\mathcal L(G)$ is not.
If $b_g\in\mathcal U(\mathcal P)$ made the new cocycle
\[
\sigma'(g,h)=b_g\alpha_g(b_h)\sigma(g,h)b_{gh}^*
\]
scalar-valued, the new action $\operatorname{Ad}_{b_g}\alpha_g$ would still preserve
the trace. Lemma~\ref{lem:scalar} would imply QWEP of $\mathcal L(G)$,
a contradiction.
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- proposition-14: body_md -->
\label{prop:translation}
For the translation action,
\[
\ell_\infty(G)\rtimes_\beta G\cong B(\ell_2(G)).
\]
Hence this ordinary crossed product is QWEP while \(\mathcal L(G)\) is non-QWEP.
<!-- end proposition-14 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
For $p_s=1_{\{s\}}$, the elements
\[
e_{s,t}=p_s\lambda(st^{-1})p_t
\]
are matrix units with $\sum_s e_{s,s}=1$ strongly and
$p_e(\ell_\infty(G)\rtimes G)p_e=\mathbb C p_e$.
Hence the crossed product is $B(\ell_2(G))$, which is injective.
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{lem:freeaction}
For every probability-measure-preserving action of a finite-rank free group on a standard probability space, \(L_\infty(X)\rtimes \mathbb F_r\) is QWEP. Freeness of the action is not required.
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
For a free basis $a_1,\ldots,a_r$,
\[
\mathcal P_X\cong *_{\mathcal A_X,\,i=1}^{r}\bigl(\mathcal A_X\rtimes\langle a_i\rangle\bigr).
\]
Indeed, alternating centered Fourier polynomials have no identity
coefficient. Each factor is an amenable crossed product of an abelian
algebra and is QWEP by \cite[Proposition~4.1\textup{(vi)}]{Ozawa04}.
Since $\mathcal A_X$ is hyperfinite, \cite[Corollary~4.5]{BDJ08} gives Connes
embeddability of $\mathcal P_X$. Apply \cite[Corollary~6.2]{Ozawa04}.
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- theorem-11: body_md -->
\label{thm:groupoid}
There is a trace-preserving isomorphism
\[
\mathcal B\rtimes_{\alpha,\Omega}\mathcal R\cong \mathcal P_X.
\]
Consequently \(\mathcal B\) and the twisted crossed product are QWEP, whereas \(\mathcal L(\mathcal R)\) is non-QWEP. This cocycle cannot be removed by a measurable field of coefficient unitaries. The same obstruction persists after tensoring each fiber with any fixed finite tracial QWEP algebra with separable predual.
<!-- end theorem-11 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
Every arrow $g:y\to x$ has the unique decomposition
\[
g=h_xt_{xy},\qquad h_x=gt_{xy}^{-1}\in H_x.
\]
For composable arrows,
\[
(h_xt_{xy})(k_yt_{yz})
=h_x\bigl(t_{xy}k_yt_{xy}^{-1}\bigr)\bigl(t_{xy}t_{yz}t_{xz}^{-1}\bigr)t_{xz}.
\]
Thus the decomposition preserves convolution, involution and the
identity-arrow trace. Passing to the regular representations gives
$\mathcal B\rtimes_{\alpha,\Omega}\mathcal R\cong \mathcal P_X$.

If coefficient unitaries removed $\Omega$, the perturbed action would
preserve the fiber traces. The untwisted crossed product would contain
$\mathcal L(\mathcal R)$ with trace-preserving expectation, contradicting
QWEP of $\mathcal P_X$. After tensoring by $\mathcal D$, the same argument applies to
$\mathcal P_X\,\overline\otimes\, \mathcal D$ and the product fiber traces.
<!-- end proof-33 -->
